dedupe_keys.name: chongqing two phase transport network for covid 19 medical waste balancing infection risk and sustainability

description: This case study optimises the transport of COVID-19 medical waste in two phases, with a choice of vehicle types, balancing infection risk, environmental risk and economic benefit. The authors, researchers at Chongqing Technology and Business University, Xiangtan University, Linköping University and the University of Oulu, formulated a mixed-integer programme, solved it with a hybrid of lexicographic optimisation and a weighted sum method, and applied it to a real case in Chongqing, China; the work is published as an open-access journal article. Coverage is province-level medical waste collection and transport in Chongqing. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: infection probabilities and weights are modelled assumptions, and results hold for the case data used. The study found that the solution strategy produced a good transport scheme within one minute, that the priority of objectives was society, then economy, then environment in both phases, and that a decentralised decision mode is preferable for designing a provincial network. Simulation uses: an optimisation template for hazardous and medical waste logistics during pandemics. Related records: the Idlib post-conflict waste network study (case_study-idlib-post-conflict-msw-network-optimisation) optimises a waste network under crisis conditions.
